note: Class: not yet attackable. Relative to STMT-CHURCH-FOUNDED-IN-COMMISSIONED-APOSTLES, Jesus' mandate and his founding of the Catholic Church as a visible society with authority, the message rival (Harnack, claim HARNACK-HOD-I-II-2-NO-NEW-COMMUNITY-PREACHING-COMMISSION) must deny that each of the four governing commissions (Matthew 16.18-19, 18.17-18, John 20.21-23, 21.15-17) goes back to Jesus (Commissions.messageRival_denies_governing_reports); it may grant Matthew 28.18-20 (Commissions.messageRival_compatible_with_mt28), and a preaching-only model fails the premise (Commissions.preachingOnly_fails_reports). The rival may instead deny STMT-CHURCH-FOUNDED-IN-COMMISSIONED-APOSTLES (the second model of Commissions.omissionModels satisfies the rival with every commission historical). The rival is not the logical negation of the premise. Harnack's note 76 (I, ch. II §3; STMT-MATT-16-18-18-17-SAYINGS-LATER) dates the words of Matthew 16.18 and 18.17 later; its event-level strengthening STMT-JUDGING-POWER-NOT-GIVEN-BY-JESUS, unattributed, refutes only the Matthew 18 commission and is compatible with this premise (CommissionAttestation.judgingPowerNotGiven_compatible). Renan (ch. XVIII; STMT-COMMUNITY-ATTRIBUTION-OF-CHURCH-POWERS-POSSIBLE) states as a possibility that many of the words on binding and remitting (Matthew 18.17 and following, John 20.23) were attributed to Jesus; no pinned source denies Matthew 16.19, 18.18, John 20.23 or 21.15-17 outright. Then, granting the link premise, Jesus' mandate and his founding of the Catholic Church as a visible society with authority, the rival must also deny STMT-JOHN-COMMISSION-INDEPENDENT-OF-MATTHEW or STMT-HEAVEN-RATIFIED-ATTESTATION-CRITERION (CATHOLICISM-MESSAGE-RIVAL-EXCLUDED-BY-ATTESTATION). Missing for an attack: a defended historical argument that at least one governing commission goes back to Jesus.
